conclusion: All 20 offline frames completed with clean safety boundaries. A 5-frame consensus grasp geometry exists in frames 9, 12, 14, 15 and 19 under the fail-closed 4-frame/25 mm/15 degree gate, but this remains an offline diagnostic and does not authorize live motion. The other IK-successful candidates (frames 11, 22 and 23) did not reach consensus.
blockers: The accepted consensus covers only 5/20 acquired frames (25%); 15 frames did not contribute to the accepted cluster.
IK-successful candidates in frames 11, 22 and 23 did not reach the 4-frame/25 mm/15 degree consensus gate.
Ten frames produced no final geometric candidate; failure reasons are multi-factor and thresholds were not relaxed.
The GraspNet checkpoint is a third-party mirror and the banana mask is a fixed HSV segmentation.
Hand-eye extrinsics, jaw clocking, shim stack, finger zero, and TCP offset are not field-validated.
Consensus is based on TCP pose and jaw symmetry, not on proof of the same contact patch or joint branch.
next_actions: Integrate the consensus gate into Task C/D mock/dry-run before considering any hardware dry-run.
Collect additional static and moved-object captures to test whether the 5-frame consensus recurs without weakening thresholds.
Keep the 4-frame minimum, 25 mm translation gate and 15 degree jaw-symmetric rotation gate fail-closed unless a separately reviewed validation set justifies a change.
Improve IK seeds for the near-convergence failures without relaxing existing position or orientation acceptance thresholds.
Complete site calibration and authorized low-speed validation before any motion authorization.
